Section 2 Site selection The aim of this script is to provide .geojson files to Planet to obtain access to high-resolution satellite data for the Western Ghats 2.1 Load necessary libraries library(sf) library(tidyverse) library(mapview) library(mapedit) library(purrr) library(terra) library(spatstat.random) # for plotting library(viridis) library(colorspace) library(scales) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork) library(fastmap) 2.2 Load the Western Ghats outline and edit it interactively to draw bounding boxes for the Nilgiris and the Anamalais wg <- st_read("data/spatial/WG.shp") wg <- st_make_valid(wg) # create bounding box/polygon interactively for the region of interest # for the sake of this exercise, we created a bounding box that is larger than the total area required for sampling # Including requests from keystone and ncf for nilgiris and anamalais str <- st_read("data/spatial/STR_boundaries.shp") atr <- st_read("data/spatial/ATR Outer boundary.geojson") area_for_editing <- mapview(str) + mapview(atr) bbox <- area_for_editing %>% editMap() # check if overall area is <15,000 sq.km st_area(bbox$finished)/ 1000000 # create files for exporting roi <- st_as_sf(bbox$finished) %>% `st_crs<-`(4326) # including shapefiles for central and northern Western Ghats mapviewOptions(fgb = FALSE) dodamarg <- st_read("data/spatial/dodamarg.shp") %>% st_zm(., drop = TRUE, what = "ZM") %>% st_make_valid() dodamarg$feature_type <- "polygon" # kadamane kadamane <- st_read("data/spatial/kadamane.geojson") %>% st_zm(., drop = TRUE, what = "ZM") %>% st_make_valid() # combining the shapefiles (combine specific rows) combined_shp <- bind_rows(roi[,2:3], dodamarg[,c(12,13)], kadamane[4,c(2,14)]) %>% filter(!is.na(geometry)) # check if overall area is <15,000 sq.km (total ~14,460) sum(st_area(combined_shp)/ 1000000) # export st_write(combined_shp, "data/spatial/western_ghats.json", driver = "GeoJSON") 2.3 Creating an interactive file to view the region of interest # to save this to a file # if you would like to share this with collaborators/colleagues html_fl <- tempfile(tmpdir = getwd(), fileext = "interactive-visualization.html") view <- mapview(wg, col.regions = "gray") + mapview(combined_shp, col.regions = "red") # create standalone .html mapview::mapshot(view, url = html_fl) view

Section 3 Code for Abi We write two ways of extracting random points, creating grids for sampling. The first method lets you interactively create the shapefile, while the second method allow you to import a shapefile and then create your random points and the grids for sampling. 3.1 Load necessary libraries library(sf) library(tidyverse) library(mapview) library(mapedit) library(purrr) library(terra) library(spatstat.random) # for plotting library(viridis) library(colorspace) library(scales) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork) library(fastmap) 3.2 Function to get EPSG codes for transformation to UTM get_utm_epsg <- function(lon, lat) { hemisphere <- ifelse(lat > 0, "N", "S") zone <- floor((lon + 180)/6) + 1 epsg <- ifelse(hemisphere == "N", paste0("326", formatC(zone, width = 2, flag = "0")), paste0("327", formatC(zone, width = 2, flag = "0"))) return(as.numeric(epsg)) } 3.3 Create the shapefile interactively and extract random points # load the required .csv of points table <- read.csv("data/test-table.csv") # extract EPSG codes and append back to the table # we will use this later for spatial transformation epsg <- mapply(get_utm_epsg, table$Longitude, table$Latitude) epsg <- data.frame(epsg) table <- bind_cols(table,epsg) # write a function so that you can process one row at a time process_single_campus <- function(row_index) { i <- row_index # convert each row to sf object point_sf <- st_as_sf(table[i,], coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326) cat("Processing:", table[i,3], "\n") # interactive edit bbox <- mapview(point_sf) %>% editMap() # create region of extent for exporting roi <- st_as_sf(bbox$finished) %>% `st_crs<-`(4326) # transform to projected system before generating random points roi <- st_transform(roi, point_sf$epsg) # generate random points using a sequential inhibition process # this works well, it should give you a warning that only x points could be placed # if it can't place more than the required number of points suggested rand_pts <- rSSI(r = 250, # minimum distance between points (here 250 mts) n = 50, # maximum number of points win = roi) # convert back to sf object rand_pts <- st_as_sf(as.data.frame(rand_pts), coords = c("x", "y"), crs = st_crs(roi)) # create a 1km x 1km grid (square) grid <- st_make_grid(x = roi, cellsize = 1000, # change cellsize accordingly square = TRUE) grid_sf <- st_sf(geometry = grid) # save shapefile with name of campus campus <- table[i,3] # create campus-specific folder campus_folder <- paste0("results/", campus) if (!dir.exists(campus_folder)) { dir.create(campus_folder, recursive = TRUE) } # write to file # write points st_write(rand_pts, paste0(campus_folder,"/", campus,"_randomPoints.shp")) # write 1km grid st_write(grid_sf, paste0(campus_folder,"/", campus, "_grid1km.shp")) # save the polygon drawn of the campus st_write(roi, paste0(campus_folder,"/", campus, "_polygonDrawn.shp")) # save .csv of latitude and longitude for the random points for collaborators rand_pts_wgs <- st_transform(rand_pts, 4326) coords <- st_coordinates(rand_pts_wgs) rand_pts_coords <- data.frame( longitude = coords[,1], latitude = coords[,2]) write.csv(rand_pts_coords, paste0(campus_folder,"/", campus, "_randomPoints.csv"), row.names = F) return(paste("Saved:", campus)) } # run manually one by one: process_single_campus(1) process_single_campus(2) # keep repeating the above until you are done with all campuses. # an example for viewing the results of what you have so far a <- st_read("results/campus1/campus1_randomPoints.shp") b <- st_read("results/campus1/campus1_grid1km.shp") c <- st_read("results/campus1/campus1_polygonDrawn.shp") d <- mapview(a, col.regions = "black") + mapview(b, col.regions = "lightgreen") + mapview(c, col.regions = "brown") d 3.4 Load the shapefile and extract points # read shapefile shapefile <- st_read("data/shapefiles/Durban_eThekwini.shp") # convert to utm # get epsg and then transform to utm coords <- st_coordinates(shapefile) pts_coords <- data.frame( longitude = coords[,1], latitude = coords[,2]) # get epsg epsg <- mapply(get_utm_epsg, pts_coords$longitude, pts_coords$latitude) # transform to projected system before generating random points roi <- st_transform(shapefile, epsg[1]) # generate random points using a sequential inhibition process # this works well, it should give you a warning that only x points could be placed # if it can't place more than the required number of points suggested rand_pts <- rSSI(r = 250, # minimum distance between points (here 250 mts) n = 50, # maximum number of points win = roi) # convert back to sf object rand_pts <- st_as_sf(as.data.frame(rand_pts), coords = c("x", "y"), crs = st_crs(roi)) # create a 1km x 1km grid (square) grid <- st_make_grid(x = roi, cellsize = 1000, # change cellsize accordingly square = TRUE) grid_sf <- st_sf(geometry = grid) # write points st_write(rand_pts, paste0("results/",campus,"_randomPoints.shp")) # change campus to some other name # write 1km grid st_write(grid_sf, paste0("results/",campus,"_grid1km.shp")) # save .csv of latitude and longitude for the random points for collaborators rand_pts_wgs <- st_transform(rand_pts, 4326) coords <- st_coordinates(rand_pts_wgs) rand_pts_coords <- data.frame( longitude = coords[,1], latitude = coords[,2]) write.csv(rand_pts_coords, paste0("results/",campus,"_randomPoints.csv"), row.names = F)
